attributes.body_ja:
助詞（じょし）「と」と「か」を組（く）み合（あ）わせた「とか」は、誰（だれ）かから聞（き）いた本当（ほんとう）かどうかははっきりしない情報（じょうほう）を伝（つた）えるときの表現（ひょうげん）です。「(A) らしい」や「(A) だそうだ」というような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

「とか」は動詞（どうし）、イ形容詞（けいようし）、ナ形容詞（けいようし）、そして名詞（めいし）の後（あと）に付（つ）けて使（つか）われます。

この意味（いみ）の「とか」はかなり砕（くだ）けた表現（ひょうげん）で、日常（にちじょう）会話（かいわ）でよく使（つか）われます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

この伝聞（でんぶん）を表（あらわ）す「とか」は、いくつかの例（れい）を挙（あ）げる「とか」と同（おな）じ形（かたち）をしています。しかし、前者（ぜんしゃ）は格助詞（かくじょし）の「と」と副助詞（ふくじょし）の「か」の組（く）み合（あ）わせ、後者（こうしゃ）は「とか」で一（ひと）つの助詞（じょし）として扱（あつか）われています。ただし、どちらも元（もと）は「と」と「か」からできているので、意味（いみ）において重（かさ）なる部分（ぶぶん）はあるでしょう。
attributes.body:
Being a combination of the particles と and か, とか 'quotes' the previous statement as being something that has been heard, but is unconfirmed or uncertain. In English, this translates as 'I heard something like (A)', or '(A) or something was said'.

とか may appear after verbs, い-Adjectives, な-Adjectives, or nouns.

This meaning of 'or something' when using とか is fairly casual and will often be heard in everyday conversation.

Caution

This combination of と and か may appear the same as the とか used to indicate lists, but the former is simply a combination of the case-marking particle と, and the adverbial particle か, while the latter is a single listing particle. Despite this, both structures are originally combinations of と and か, and may be thought to have some overlap in meaning.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: とか vs. って vs. という vs. と言われている

attributes.body: Both can report hearsay, but with different tone. とか is casual and vague, often implying uncertainty, similar to 'I heard / They say (A), or something.' ということだ is more formal and declarative, closer to 'The word is (A).' ということだ can also be used to draw conclusions (i.e. 'that means (A)'), which とか cannot.

first_relatable.title: とか
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that… something like, They said ... or something

second_relatable.title: ということだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, Rumor has it that, It is said that, It means that

attributes.body: Both can relay hearsay, but with different levels of certainty. とか adds a nuance of vagueness or uncertainty, e.g. 来月引っ越すとか ('I heard they might be moving next month, or something.') そうだ also conveys hearsay, but with less ambiguity, e.g. 来月引っ越すそうだ ('I heard they're moving next month.')

first_relatable.title: とか
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that… something like, They said ... or something

second_relatable.title: そうだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, It is said that

attributes.body: These two expressions are similar in that both can serve as casual expressions of hearsay, i.e. 'they say (A)' or 'I hear (A)'. The difference is that んだって has a slightly more explanatory and emphatic nuance due to the presence of ん, while とか has an uncertain or non-specific tone, i.e. 'I hear (A) or something', because of the presence of the question particle か.

first_relatable.meaning: I heard that, He or She said that
